idiom_name: Step type + id union derived from a registry object (keyof typeof), cursor loop
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds a compile-time contract to the JavaScript idiom: type the step as (env: Envelope) => Promise<Envelope>, keep the registry as a const object checked with satisfies Record<string, Step>, and derive the itinerary's legal values with keyof typeof registry - the slip field is then a union of real step ids, so a planner that names a non-existent step fails to compile instead of at 3 a.m. That type-level registry replaces the classic Router/Step classes; Koa/Express middleware remains the framework cousin whose order is fixed at startup. Use branded ids or a discriminated union when two steps share a signature, and keep the envelope generic so steps can narrow the payload type.
pitfalls: A registry typed as Record<string, Step> erases the ids and lets typos compile; derive StepId with keyof typeof and keep the object literal inline.
Structural typing makes any two same-signature steps interchangeable, so accidental swaps pass the compiler - brand step ids when the order is safety-critical.
Promise rejections truncate the itinerary silently unless every step is wrapped: model failures as a Result-like union or catch per step before advancing.
JSON.parse of an incoming slip yields string, not StepId; validate it against the registry keys at the boundary or the type lie reaches production.
